blocks.title: Four plants, four systems
blocks.body: Each site ran its own mix of spreadsheets and legacy tools — the same part could carry three different numbers depending on who you asked.

blocks.title: No shared truth
blocks.body: Head office consolidated production and stock figures by hand, weeks after the fact, and planned against data that was already stale.

blocks.title: A hard deadline
blocks.body: A new distribution contract required unified stock visibility within one quarter — the rollout had a twelve-week window, not a twelve-month one.

blocks.title: No room for downtime
blocks.body: Lines run around the clock. A cutover that stopped production for even a shift was off the table.

blocks.title: One ERPNext instance
blocks.body: A single, opinionated configuration — shared item masters, BOMs, and costing — replacing four divergent ways of working with one.

blocks.title: Telemetry into the ERP
blocks.body: Gateways on the plant floor stream machine counts and states into ERPNext, so work orders close themselves against reality.

blocks.title: Plant-by-plant cutover
blocks.body: Each plant ran two weeks in parallel before switching — issues surfaced against live data without risking production.

blocks.title: Trained on their own data
blocks.body: Operators and planners learned the system on their own parts and orders, not demo data — adoption came with the rollout, not after it.

blocks.title: Weeks 1–3 · Discovery
blocks.body: Process mapping across all four sites, one canonical item master, and a migration plan agreed with every plant manager.

blocks.title: Weeks 4–8 · Build
blocks.body: Configuration, custom integrations to MES and label systems, and telemetry gateways installed line by line.

blocks.title: Weeks 9–12 · Cutover
blocks.body: Parallel running, data migration, and go-live one plant per week — the fourth plant switched on schedule, day 84.

blocks.title: After go-live
blocks.body: Hypercare on-site through the first close, then a quarterly roadmap of refinements driven by floor feedback.
